rv.q: Consistently over-the-top with plenty of laughs and some technical dash for which the Road has long been known, Sawyer's production shoots out a volley of satirical darts, few of which land with much impact.
Kaiju is an accomplished and entertaining production that proves once again how lucky we are to have The Road Theatre doing its thing in L.A. This show is a blast.

Adventurous, hilarious, and unhinged plays used to be a regular occurrence in the LA theater scene. Is KAIJU a hint that audiences will come back to plays that make us laugh at ourselves, sensitivity be damned? I sure hope so.
Kaiju by Dan Caffrey is a thoroughly enjoyable satire about any and all discourse to do with art.
Kaiju may not float everyone's boat, but if schlocky monster movies are your thing and you enjoy it when theater gets meta, you'll likely have as good a time at the Road as I did on opening night.
